theater: 美吉多山口與北敘利亞

battle.name: 第二次敘利亞戰役
battle.theater: 美吉多山口與北敘利亞
battle.brief: 公元前1457年，埃及新王國法老圖特摩斯三世率軍北上，於美吉多山口與卡迭施王為首的敘利亞—迦南聯軍遭遇，雙方各出約千輛戰車，是有可靠記載以來最大的車戰。聯軍崩潰、退入城中，埃及人攻圍七個月後迫其投降。卡面埃及長矛是這支軍隊的近身兵器：弓兵車兵撕開缺口，長矛方陣與彎斧完成廝殺。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 第二次敘利亞戰役是埃及新王國與敘利亞、迦南諸邦聯盟之間的一場戰爭，時間通常定在公元前1458年至1456年。埃及一方以第十八王朝法老圖特摩斯三世為最高統帥，宮廷照例設有丞相（維齊爾）與王室書記官，軍隊由步兵（射手與持矛的「強臂」）、車兵，以及隨軍的努比亞人與麥德雅民兵組成，另有供水、搬運、築壘的隨行人員；指揮系統極簡，戰術決斷與全軍突擊都由國王本人作出，王室軍事書記官塔雅內尼以羊皮紙逐日記錄行程與戰果，數十年後由工匠刻上卡納克阿蒙神廟的「編年史牆」。聯盟一方以卡迭施王為首，集合阿勒頗、圖尼普、努哈希什等地的諸王，以及埃及在阿穆魯地區的附庸，美吉多王是其中最積極的成員，聯軍在美吉多城內集結，主力則佈置在沿海的塔阿納赫一帶水源地。聯盟背後有米坦尼的支援，希梯與巴比倫初期按兵不動，卡納克牆上把巴比倫、亞述、希梯送來的禮物一律記作「進貢」。戰爭的導火線是哈特謝普蘇特的去世：埃及在敘利亞的督政與徵收體系一度鬆動，附庸王乘機舉兵。戰後埃及並未吞併這些邦國，而是改為每年收取貢賦、扣留王子作人質的附庸體系。
countriesEn: The Second Syrian War was a conflict between the Egyptian New Kingdom and a coalition of Syrian and Canaanite states, conventionally dated to about 1458–1456 BC. On the Egyptian side stood the Eighteenth Dynasty under Pharaoh Thutmose III (Menkheperre), the supreme commander, with the usual court apparatus of a vizier and royal scribes. His army combined infantry — archers together with the spearmen of the sphtm, the 'strong arm' — with a chariot corps and with Nubian and Medjay auxiliaries, plus water carriers, porters and siege labour. The command structure was austere: the king himself made the tactical decisions and led the general assault, while a military scribe named Tjaneni (Thanuny) kept a day-by-day journal on parchment which, decades later, was carved onto the Hall of Annals of the temple of Amun-Re at Karnak. The coalition was headed by the king of Kadesh and drew in the princes of Aleppo, Tunip and Nuhashe together with Egypt's own Amurru vassals; the king of Megiddo was among the most committed participants. The rebels concentrated inside Megiddo, while the main body of their host was posted around the waters of Taanach on the coastal plain. Mitanni backed the revolt from behind, while Hatti and Babylonia held themselves apart at first; gifts from Babylon, Assyria and Hatti were later entered on the Karnak wall as 'tribute'. The occasion of the war was the death of Hatshepsut: the Egyptian administrative and tribute-collecting machine in Syria loosened for a time, and the vassal kings rose. Egypt did not annex the Syrian states after the victory; it converted them into a tribute-paying vassal system with princes held at the Egyptian court.
people: 法老圖特摩斯三世是這場戰爭的核心人物。他在位的第二十一年，母親哈特謝普蘇特於第六月十日去世（阿爾曼特石碑記其卒日），他隨即獨自執掌王權，此後卻把整個統治重心都用在連年北征上。軍中為他記錄戰況的是王室軍事書記官塔雅內尼，他以羊皮紙寫成的逐日日誌是本場戰爭唯一的第一手記錄；約在圖特摩斯三世第三十二年，他命工匠把這些紀功刻上卡納克阿蒙神廟的編年史牆，留下奪車、虜人、納貢的清單。敵方領袖方面，卡迭施王是聯軍的實際統帥，美吉多王與他共同守城，兩王都在城破前逃入美吉多；卡納克的浮雕與銘文留下圖特摩斯三世策馬擊殺敵將的畫面。據記載，圖特摩斯三世在進攻美吉多前先遣斥候探路，將領力勸他走較安全的沿海大路，他卻選了最險的阿魯納狹谷，並親自率先鋒開道。米坦尼國王沒有留下名字，但兩百餘年後以書信與埃及交涉的圖舒拉塔是這個王朝後來的君主，兩朝的往來信件至今仍存。埃及朝廷之中，丞相乃西是國王的主要行政依靠；宮廷畫師在雷赫米爾墓中畫下「列特努首長」進貢的場面，長矛、弓與弓弦盒一併畫入，成為這場戰爭留在埃及藝術裡最生動的一頁。
peopleEn: Pharaoh Thutmose III is the central figure of the war. In the twenty-first year of his reign his mother Hatshepsut died on the tenth day of the sixth month, as recorded by the stela from Armant, and he took sole control of the state; from then on the whole weight of his government was spent on annual campaigns to the north. The man who recorded what happened was the royal military scribe Tjaneni, whose day-by-day journal on parchment is the only first-hand account of the campaign. Around the thirty-second year of the reign the king ordered the exploits carved onto the Hall of Annals of Amun-Re at Karnak, where the lists of captured chariots, prisoners and tribute were set down. On the enemy side the king of Kadesh was the effective commander of the coalition; the king of Megiddo shared the defence of the city with him, and both kings escaped into Megiddo before it fell. The reliefs and inscriptions at Karnak preserve the image of Thutmose III in his chariot smiting the enemy prince. According to the record, the king sent out scouts before moving on Megiddo; his officers urged him to take the safer coast road, and he chose instead the dangerous Aruna ravine, leading the advance himself. The king of Mitanni left no name, but Tushratta, who corresponded with Egypt by letter more than two centuries later, was a later ruler of that dynasty, and the correspondence of the two courts survives. At the Egyptian court the vizier Nahsi was the king's chief administrative support; the tomb of Rekhmire shows the 'chiefs of Retjenu' bringing tribute, and spears, bows and bow cases are all painted into the scene, making it the most vivid page this war left behind in Egyptian art.
kits: 卡面上的埃及長矛是這支軍隊的標準近身兵器。早王朝時期以銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上的形制，到新王國已定型為約二公尺至二公尺半的直杆：杆身取硬木，前段裝套筒式銅或青銅矛頭，尾端加配重，握處常纏皮帶。圖特摩斯三世的美吉多大軍中，長矛是步兵「強臂」的主兵器，與彎斧並列；弓兵與車兵在山口撕開聯軍正面，長矛方陣與彎斧才完成貼身的廝殺。美吉多圍城歷時七個月，埃及人築壕溝、豎木柵、動手破壞城內水源，長矛同時是工兵攀登與破壞柵牆的工具。除長矛外，這場戰爭用到的裝備還有：以角、腱與木料製成的複合弓，箭鏃為青銅或燧石；六輻輕型戰車，每車一御者一射手，駕四匹馬，車前欄板與弓兵位；青銅鎬形斧與單刃彎斧；皮革包木框的盾牌；營帳、旗幟與飾有「聖蛇」紋的王家標幟。軍隊還攜帶牛拉駁船，以便在無水路段把船隻搬過陸地，而水罐與馱隊的長度，直接決定了這支遠征軍能走多遠。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card was the standard close-combat arm of this army. The early dynastic form, a copper or bronze head bound to a wooden shaft, had by the New Kingdom settled into a straight shaft some two to two and a half metres long: hardwood, with a socketed copper or bronze head at the front, a counterweight at the base, and grip bindings of leather. In Thutmose III's army at Megiddo the spear was the principal weapon of the sphtm, the infantry 'strong arm', standing beside the khopesh axe; the archers and the chariots tore open the front of the coalition line, and only the spear ranks and the axes finished the work at close quarters. The siege of Megiddo lasted seven months: the Egyptians dug a ditch, raised a wooden palisade and damaged the water supply inside the city, and the spear doubled as a tool for sappers climbing and breaking the defences. Alongside the spear, the equipment of this war included the composite bow built of horn, sinew and wood, with bronze or flint arrowheads; the six-spoked light war chariot carrying a driver and an archer and drawn by four horses, with a front rail and a bowman's position; bronze pickaxes and single-edged khopesh axes; shields of leather over a wooden frame; and tents, standards and the royal banner marked with the uraeus. The army also carried ox-drawn boats so that vessels could be hauled overland where no water route existed, and the length of the water jars and pack trains directly set the limit on how far this expeditionary force could march.
tactics: 圖特摩斯三世的戰術核心是速度、出其不意與集中車兵衝擊。全軍在邊境要塞提亞魯集結，於第八月二十五日出發，經加薩抵達耶海姆；抵達前先遣斥候探明三條北上路線：北線經宰夫提與約克尼安，南線經塔阿納赫，中線則是狹窄的阿魯納谷，即阿拉谷。將領力勸走較安全的南北兩路，圖特摩斯卻反其道而行，親自帶領輕步兵與騎射的「哈伊布拉」清掉谷口哨兵，主力車隊魚貫而出，進入耶斯德列谷的平原。當夜他把大軍調到與敵相對的位置，黎明發動攻擊，陣線排成三翼、略呈凹形，兩翼挾住聯軍兩側，國王自居中央。聯軍車兵密集而難以展開，埃及車兵由左翼沿坡地展開，一接觸便深入敵陣，捲起的塵土使雙方都難看清戰況，聯軍陣線當場崩潰，士兵湧入美吉多城並關上城門。埃及人先搶掠敵營，奪得九百二十四輛戰車與二百套鎧甲；卡迭施王與美吉多王趁亂逃入城內，守軍用衣物結繩把人與車吊上城頭。接下來是長達七個月的圍城：挖壕溝、豎木柵、切斷城內水源，最終迫其投降，卻保留了城與居民。
tacticsEn: The core of Thutmose III's tactical method was speed, surprise and the massed chariot charge. The army mustered at the border fortress of Tjaru and set out on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month, moving through Gaza to Yehem; before arriving he sent scouts ahead to test the three roads north: the northern route by way of Zefti and Yokneam, the southern route past Taanach, and the central route through the narrow Aruna ravine, the Wadi Ara. His officers urged the safer northern or southern road, and he did the opposite, leading the light infantry and the mounted bowmen, the haibrw, personally to clear the pickets at the mouth of the pass while the main body of chariots followed in single file and spilled out onto the plain of Esdraelon. During the night he drew the army up opposite the enemy, and at dawn attacked with the line in three wings, slightly concave, the two wings threatening the flanks of the coalition while the king held the centre. The allied chariots were massed too tightly to manoeuvre; the Egyptians deployed down the slope on the left, drove straight into the enemy ranks the moment they touched, and the dust raised by the fighting made it hard for either side to see. The coalition line collapsed on the spot, its men pouring into Megiddo and shutting the gates behind them. The Egyptians fell to plundering the camp and took 924 chariots and 200 suits of armour; the kings of Kadesh and Megiddo escaped into the city, where the defenders lowered ropes of knotted clothing and hauled men and chariots up onto the walls. What followed was a siege of seven months: a ditch dug, a palisade raised, the city's water supply cut, and finally a surrender that nevertheless left the town and its inhabitants in being.
data: 日期方面：哈特謝普蘇特卒於圖特摩斯三世第二十一年第六月十日；大軍於第八月二十五日自提亞魯出發，十日後抵加薩，休息一日，再走十一日於第九月中旬抵達耶海姆；美吉多之戰記在第二十三年第三季第一月第二十一日，即新月祭之日，按低年代換算為公元前1457年5月9日，亦有出版物定於同年4月16日，更早的年表則把整場戰爭放在公元前1482年或1479年。兵力方面，卡納克編年史記埃及方面二萬人、一千輛戰車，聯軍方面估計一萬至一萬五千人；學者雷德福的估算則是雙方各約一萬零五百至一萬零八百人，戰車各約一千輛。繳獲清單為：俘虜三百四十人、母馬二千零四十一匹、幼馬一百九十一匹、種馬六匹、戰車九百二十四輛、鎧甲二百套、弓五百零二張、牛一千九百二十九頭、綿羊二萬二千五百隻，並有美吉多王的王家鎧甲、戰車與帳桿。圍城歷時七個月，亦有記為七至八個月。全役合計記錄圖特摩斯三世十七次遠征，其中十四次刻於卡納克；美吉多之戰也是有可靠文字記載以來最早留下傷亡數字的會戰，並被視為複合弓的第一次有記載的實戰使用。
dataEn: On dates: Hatshepsut died on the tenth day of the sixth month of Thutmose III's twenty-first year; the army set out on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month from Tjaru, reached Gaza ten days later, rested one day and marched a further eleven days to arrive at Yehem in the middle of the ninth month; the battle of Megiddo is dated to the twenty-first day of the first month of the third season of year 23, the day of the feast of the new moon, which on the low chronology converts to 9 May 1457 BC, while some publications place it on 16 April of the same year and older chronologies put the whole war in 1482 or 1479 BC. On numbers of men: the Karnak annals give 20,000 men and 1,000 chariots for the Egyptians, and estimate the coalition at 10,000 to 15,000; the estimate of Redford puts both sides at roughly 10,500 to 10,800 men with about 1,000 chariots each. The booty list reads: 340 prisoners, 2,041 mares, 191 foals, 6 stallions, 924 chariots, 200 suits of armour, 502 bows, 1,929 cattle, 22,500 sheep, together with the royal armour, chariot and tent-poles of the king of Megiddo. The siege lasted seven months, though seven or eight are both recorded. The war as a whole accounts for 17 campaigns of Thutmose III, 14 of which are carved at Karnak; Megiddo is among the earliest battles to survive with explicit casualty figures, and is treated as the first recorded use of the composite bow in battle.
cause: 起因有遠近兩層。遠因是埃及自第十八王朝立國以來，靠圖特摩斯二世時期的第一次敘利亞戰爭在敘利亞南部取得立足點，並以加薩至比布魯斯一線的「海道」與內陸商路為生命線，附庸邦國按年進貢，這套體系需要一位能年年北征的國王來維繫。近因是圖特摩斯三世即位時年紀尚輕，母親哈特謝普蘇特攝政，其卒後數十年間，埃及在北方的督政官員與駐軍一度收縮，徵貢減弱；卡迭施王判斷新君軟弱，率先脫離，其他城邦隨之舉兵，美吉多王加入聯盟，並把聯軍主力集結在塔阿納赫一帶水源地，擺出迎戰姿態，實際上是希望在新王尚未站穩之前把埃及勢力逐出迦南。這場叛亂的算盤是：只要擋住美吉多這個通往幼發拉底河的關口，埃及在亞洲的霸權就會自行瓦解。史料亦指出聯軍背後有米坦尼在推動，敘利亞諸王多與米坦尼的胡里安貴族往來密切；希梯與巴比倫各有算計，初期並未直接出兵相助。於是一場原本屬於宮廷的王位繼承事件，最終變成了兩國在黎凡特全面較量的導火線。
causeEn: The causes work on two levels, near and far. The distant cause is that Egypt, since the founding of the Eighteenth Dynasty, had won a foothold in southern Syria during the First Syrian War of the reign of Thutmose II, and made the Via Maris, the coast road from Gaza to Byblos, together with the inland caravan routes, its lifeline; the vassal states paid tribute year by year, and that system required a king able to campaign north every single year to hold it together. The proximate cause is that Thutmose III came to the throne young, with his mother Hatshepsut holding the regency; in the years after her death the Egyptian officials and garrisons in the north contracted for a time and tribute collection weakened. The king of Kadesh judged the new king weak and broke away first, other cities followed, and the king of Megiddo joined the coalition, posting the main rebel host around the waters of Taanach in what was essentially a challenge to arms, the real intention being to drive Egyptian power out of Canaan before the new king had established himself. The arithmetic of the revolt was simple: block the pass at Megiddo, the gateway to the Euphrates, and Egypt's Asian supremacy would unravel of its own accord. The sources also show Mitanni pushing from behind, with the Syrian princes in close contact with the Hurrian nobility of that state; Hatti and Babylonia each pursued their own interest and at first did not intervene with troops. A succession affair that began inside the palace thus became the fuse for a general confrontation between two powers in the Levant.
impact: 影響是深遠的。美吉多一役之後，埃及重新控制迦南北部，取得美吉多這個扼守「海道」與耶斯德列谷的關口，並在城內留下駐軍，把一場開放的戰爭變成常態化的帝國邊防。圖特摩斯三世沒有把敘利亞諸邦直接併入版圖，而是改用附庸體系：各城按年進貢，王子與貴族子弟被帶往埃及宮廷接受教育，日後回國治理，成為埃及文化的代理人。這套扣留人質的辦法在往後二十年屢見不鮮，也是日後阿馬爾納書信時代國際秩序的雛形。制度層面，埃及由此確立了以步兵、弓兵與車兵為主幹的常備軍，固定的北征季節、統一的行軍與供水制度，以及王室對戰功的直接記錄與宣傳，使國王本人成為軍隊的宣傳核心，軍功成了王權合法性的來源。對外格局上，埃及的聲勢越過幼發拉底河，亞述、巴比倫、希梯先後送來禮物，卡納克牆上把這些禮物改寫成「進貢」；唯一不肯低頭的是米坦尼，雙方的對抗延續到圖特摩斯三世去世以後，結下百年之敵。長期後果是地名的魔力：美吉多之名逐步被引申為世界末日戰場的代號，「哈米吉多頓」成為跨越兩千年、跨越信仰的末日預言之名。
impactEn: The consequences were far-reaching. After Megiddo Egypt regained control of northern Canaan, took the city that commands the Via Maris and the Jezreel valley, and left a garrison inside it, converting a single open war into a permanent imperial frontier. Thutmose III did not annex the Syrian states outright; he substituted a vassal system in which each city paid tribute annually and princes and noble children were taken to the Egyptian court to be educated, later returning to rule their own lands as agents of Egyptian culture. This habit of holding hostages recurs throughout the following twenty years and is the embryo of the international order of the Amarna letter age. Institutionally, Egypt now possessed a standing army built on infantry, archers and chariots, a fixed campaigning season, a unified march and water-supply system, and a royal apparatus for recording and publicising the war, which made the king himself the focus of the army's propaganda and turned military achievement into a source of royal legitimacy. In the wider world Egyptian prestige pushed past the Euphrates: Assyria, Babylonia and Hatti sent gifts in turn, and the Karnak wall rewrote those gifts as 'tribute'. Only Mitanni refused to bow, and the rivalry between the two courts outlived Thutmose III, leaving a hundred-year enmity behind. The most durable legacy is the magic of the place-name: Megiddo was gradually extended into a byword for the battle at the end of the world, and 'Armageddon' passed from one millennium to the next as a name for the last battle, across every faith.
result: 結果是埃及的全面勝利。聯軍在美吉多城外崩潰，戰車九百二十四輛被擄，兩王逃入城中；七個月的圍城之後，美吉多開城投降，城市與居民得保，埃及人只帶走財物與俘虜，聯軍各城隨後一個個遣使請和，開始按年進貢，並送王子入埃及為質。此後數年，圖特摩斯三世又發動第五、第六、第七次遠征，掃平西姆拉、烏拉扎、阿爾達塔等腓尼基與內陸城市，沒收當地穀倉，運糧到海港供應駐軍，藉此斷掉叛亂的財源；其後更北上攻取卡爾凱美什，並在第三十三年造舟西行至比布魯斯，把船隻搬過陸地後強渡幼發拉底河，讓米坦尼國王措手不及。第十次遠征與阿勒頗附近的交戰，卡納克只記十名俘虜，可能是打成平手；最後一次亞洲遠征雖然掃平阿爾干圖平原與圖尼普，仍未能攻下卡迭施。戰爭最終以埃及與米坦尼在幼發拉底河一線達成和約收場：雙方交換了記載條款的「書」與銀器，邊界大致維持在歐朗特斯河與幼發拉底河之間，埃及終究未能吞併米坦尼，此後百年雙方在這條河上反覆爭鬥，而埃及在黎凡特的霸主地位則由此奠定，成為卡納克戰功記載中最輝煌的一章。
resultEn: The result was a complete Egyptian victory. The coalition collapsed outside Megiddo, 924 of its chariots were taken, and the two kings fled into the city; after seven months of siege Megiddo opened its gates and surrendered, the town and its inhabitants were spared, and the Egyptians carried off only goods and prisoners. The cities of the coalition sent embassies one after another, began paying tribute by the year, and handed over princes to be held at the Egyptian court. In the years that followed, Thutmose III launched his fifth, sixth and seventh campaigns, sweeping the Phoenician and inland cities of Simyra, Ullaza and Ardata, confiscating the local grain stores and moving the grain to the harbours to provision the garrisons, so as to cut off the money that had financed the revolts. He then drove north to take Carchemish, and in year 33 he had ships built at the coast and carried them overland before force-crossing the Euphrates, taking the king of Mitanni by surprise. The tenth campaign and the fighting near Aleppo are entered in the Karnak annals with only ten prisoners, and may have ended in stalemate; the last Asian campaign cleared the plain of Arkanṭu and Tunip but still did not take Kadesh. The war closed with a peace between Egypt and Mitanni on the line of the Euphrates: the two sides exchanged a 'book' recording the terms together with silver vessels, the frontier broadly held between the Orontes and the Euphrates, and Egypt never swallowed Mitanni whole. The two states would fight over that river for the next hundred years, but Egypt's position as the hegemon of the Levant was now established, and the campaigns at Karnak record it as the most glorious chapter of the king's titulary.
